translations.text: The story of Saint Matthew and Saint Andrew, the blessed apostles.
Again, the story of Saint Matthew and Saint Andrew, the blessed apostles, when they made disciples in the city of Kalbin, whose inhabitants ate human flesh.
After the days of the ascension of our Lord Jesus Christ into heaven, when the days of Pentecost were fulfilled,
the Comforter came to the upper room of Zion, and the holy apostles were filled with the gift of the Holy Spirit.
Each one of them wished to go out and proclaim the good news of Christ. They began casting lots and dividing the regions among themselves.
And when they had [?], it fell to Matthew the apostle to go to the city whose inhabitants ate human beings.
The inhabitants of that city ate no bread and drank no water.
Instead, their food was human flesh, and their drink was human blood.
Every person whom [?], they would gouge out his eyes and give him a cup to drink that had been mixed with sorcery.
As soon as he drank that cup, his heart would change, he would lose his understanding, and he would acquire the heart of a beast.
When Saint Matthew entered through the city gate, he was seized
by the inhabitants of that city. They gouged out his eyes and gave him that cup to drink which had been mixed with sorcery.
They took him to the prison where everyone who fell into their hands was confined.
They would throw him straw to eat. But when the blessed apostle drank the cup they gave him, his heart did not change.
Instead, he remained constantly in prayer and unceasing tears, saying, “Our Lord Jesus Christ, for whose sake we have left everything and followed you,
because we know that you are the true God, the helper and savior of all who hope in you: look, my Lord, and see what this wicked people has done to Matthew your servant,
how they have made me like a beast without understanding. For you know everything.
If, my Lord, it is your will that I should become food for the inhabitants of this city, let your will be done. I do not flee from your command.
Give me the light of my eyes so that I may see what the people of this city are doing to me. Do not abandon me, my Lord, or hand me over to this bitter death.”
While the blessed Matthew was praying these things, a brilliant light shone throughout the place where he was confined.
A voice was heard from that light, saying, “Matthew, my apostle, lift up your eyes.”
Immediately he lifted his eyes and saw. The voice came to him again a second time and said, “Matthew, stand firm and be strong
and do not be afraid. For I will neither forsake you nor abandon you. I will rescue you from every trial—not you alone, but all your companions as well.
For I am with you at all times. Now endure twenty-five days in this prison for the benefit of many souls.
After these days I will send Andrew to you, and he will bring you out of this prison, together with everyone who is here with you.”
When our Savior had said these things, he ascended to heaven. Then Matthew said, “May your grace be with us, our Lord Jesus Christ.”
He was inside the prison, murmuring. And when the guards would enter the prison
to bring people out for slaughter, Matthew would close his eyes so that they would not realize that he could see the light.
And on one of the following days, we will bring this man out too and slaughter him. For they would write on a wooden tablet the day on which a person was arrested and tie it to his hand,
so that they would know when his days were completed. And when twenty-seven days had passed since blessed Matthew was arrested,
our Lord Jesus Christ appeared to Andrew in the place where he was teaching and said to him, “Andrew, get up and go with your disciples
to the city whose inhabitants eat human beings.
Bring Matthew out of the prison where he is. For in three days those wicked people are going to bring him out and slaughter him for their food.”
Andrew answered and said, “My Lord, I cannot reach that city within three days, because the journey is long.
Instead, send an angel to bring him out of there. For you know, my Lord, that I am clothed in a body, and I cannot get there quickly.
I do not even know the way.” But our Lord answered and said to him, “Andrew, listen and obey the one who made you and brought you into being.
For he can give a command in the blink of an eye, and that city will be lifted up and brought here. For I command the wind, and it will bring you there.
But get up in the morning and go down to the seashore with your disciples, and there you will find a boat. Board it, you and your disciples.”
When our Lord had said these things, he gave him a greeting of peace and ascended to [?]. Then Andrew got up in the morning as he had been commanded,
and went to the seashore with his disciples. He saw a small boat, and three men were sitting in the boat.
For our Lord himself had prepared a boat by his command, and he appeared in it in the form of a sailor. With him were two angels in human form.
When Andrew saw that boat and the three men in it, he rejoiced greatly. He approached the boat and said
to them, “Where are you going, my brothers?” Our Lord said to him, “We are going to the land where they eat human beings.”
But Andrew did not realize that it was Jesus. Our Lord had concealed the might of his divine power and appeared as a helmsman.
Andrew answered and said, “We too want to go to that city.”
Then our Lord said to him, “Everyone flees from that city, and you want to go there?” Andrew answered and said,
“We have something to do there, and we must go there. Now, if you will do us a kindness, let us know.” Jesus answered and said to them,
“Come aboard in peace.” Andrew answered and said, “My brother, I want you to know, before we board the boat,
that we have no fare to give you for the boat, nor do we have any bread with us to eat.” Our Lord said to him, “And how can you board the boat
when you have no fare with you?” Andrew said to him, “Listen, my brother. Do not think that it is out of stubbornness that we are not giving you the fare for the boat.
But we are disciples of our Lord Jesus Christ, who loved us and chose us, the Twelve, and gave us a command, saying:
“When you go out to preach, do not take purses or traveling bags with you,
nor copper money in your purses, nor bread, nor a staff, nor sandals. And you are not to have two tunics
with you.” So if you will show us mercy, tell us quickly. Otherwise, we will look for another boat.
Jesus answered them, “If this is the command you received and you keep it, come aboard.
For I told you that I am more eager for Christ’s disciples to board my boat than for those who give me gold and silver.
But I tell you this: perhaps I am worthy to have a disciple of Christ board my boat.” Andrew answered,
“Forgive me, my brother. May our Lord give you a reward and forgiveness.” Then Andrew boarded the boat and said to his disciples,
“My children, if you wish, remain on dry land until I complete what our Lord has commanded me and return to you.” But his disciples said to him, “Far be it from us to do this!
For if we stay behind without you, we become strangers to the grace given to us. Now we will be with you wherever you go.”
Then Jesus answered Andrew, “If you truly are a disciple of Christ,
remind your disciples of the mighty deeds your master did, to give them courage so that they forget their anxiety about this sea.
For we are now ready to release the boat from the shore and sail.” Andrew encouraged his disciples, saying, “My children, you have surrendered
your lives for Christ’s sake. Do not be afraid. For he did not abandon us at that time when we were with him in the boat,
and he was sleeping in the boat while testing you. For he was not really asleep. And when a great wind arose and the sea raised its waves
so that they rose above the boat’s timbers, great fear seized us. Our Savior arose and rebuked the wind, and the waves subsided, and there was a great calm on the sea.
For everything obeys his command, because they are his creation. And now, my children, do not be afraid.” When Andrew had said these things,
he prayed that his disciples would remain at peace. When they fell asleep, Andrew turned and said to Jesus,
not knowing that it was Jesus, “Tell me, man, and explain to me truthfully this skill of yours in steering.
For I have never seen a pilot steer a boat as I now see you doing.
I have sailed on the sea sixteen times, and this is the seventeenth, but I have never seen skill like this.
For truly this boat is as much at ease in the middle of the sea as on dry land. Explain your skill to us, young man.” Then our Lord said to Andrew,
“We too have sailed on the sea many times, and a fierce storm has risen against us. But because you are a disciple of Christ,
the sea recognized you and did not raise its waves against us.” Then Andrew cried out in a loud voice, saying, “I bless

your name, my Lord Jesus Christ, because you have brought me to meet a man who praises your name.” Jesus answered him, “Tell me, disciple of Jesus, why did the wicked Jews not believe that your master is the true God?”
Show me. But we have heard that he showed his power to his disciples.” Andrew answered and said:
“Yes, my brother, he showed us that he is the true God. And now do not think that Jesus is not God.
For he made humankind.” Jesus answered and said, “Then why did the Jews not believe in him?” Andrew answered and said:
“O man who has a spirit of knowledge and every kind of understanding, why are you testing me?” Our Lord said to him, “I am not testing you with these things.
Rather, my soul is glad and rejoices in them.” Andrew said, “My brother, may the Lord fill your soul with great joy and grace.” Then our Lord answered and said:
“Then tell me.” Andrew answered and said, “Have you not heard of the mighty works he did before them? He gave sight to the blind,
and enabled the lame to walk and the deaf and mute to hear and speak. He drove out demons, cleansed lepers, and raised the dead to life.
He changed water into wine. He took five loaves and two fish and commanded the crowd to recline on the grass.
He blessed them and fed the people until they were satisfied. Five thousand ate and were satisfied, and they had some left over. And again he pronounced a blessing
over seven loaves and fed four thousand until they were satisfied. He performed many signs, wonders, and mighty works,
which, if I recounted them before you, you could not bear.” Jesus said to him, “Indeed I could. But one word is enough for a wise person, while even many words do not persuade a fool.”
When our Lord knew that the boat had reached the appointed place on land, he inclined his head toward one of the angels,
and stopped speaking with Andrew. When Andrew saw this, he leaned over toward his disciples and sank into a heavy sleep.
Our Lord said to the angels, “Put your hands together, lift up Andrew and his disciples, and go and set them down at the gate of the city whose inhabitants eat human flesh.”
The angels did as they had been commanded. They lifted up Andrew and his disciples, carried them away, and set them down at the gate of the city whose inhabitants eat human beings.
When Andrew awoke from his sleep and opened his eyes, he saw that he was sitting at the gate of that city, with his disciples asleep beside him.
While he was marveling at what had happened, he woke them and said to them, “Get up, my children, and see the favor that has been shown to us.
Know that our Lord was with us in the boat, testing us, and we did not recognize him.” His disciples answered and said to him, “Do not think, our father,
that we knew we were sailing on the sea, for we were sunk in a deep sleep. We saw angels come and take our souls and carry them to paradise.
There we saw great wonders. For we saw our Lord Jesus Christ sitting on a glorious throne,
with all the angels looking at him. There we also saw Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the fathers and holy prophets,
and you, the twelve apostles, standing beside our Lord Jesus Christ. We heard our Lord commanding his holy angels:
‘Obey the apostles in everything they tell you.’ This is the vision we saw, our father.” Then blessed Andrew,
when he heard these things from his disciples, rejoiced greatly because his disciples had been found worthy to see the great things of God.
He lifted his eyes to heaven and said, “Pardon me, my Lord, and forgive me for what I have done.
For I saw you as a man in the boat, and I spoke with you as a man. What sin have I committed, my Lord? You did not show me your greatness.” And our Lord said to him:
“You have not sinned, Andrew. But I did these things for you because you said, ‘I cannot reach the city of the dogs in three days.’
Now I have shown you that I have the power to do everything. But get up and enter the city, going to your brother Matthew. Bring him out of prison,
along with everyone imprisoned with him. And now, before you enter their city, I am telling you that they will inflict severe suffering on you, and your body will be torn apart.
Your blood will be poured out on the ground like water. They cannot put you to death, but many sufferings are going to come upon you.
But endure, and do not resist their wickedness. Remember the sufferings I endured when the Jews were striking me and spitting in my face.
Could I not have shaken heaven and earth in the blink of an eye and brought suffering upon those who struck me? But I endured and forgave them, to show you an example.”
Andrew immediately got up and entered that city with his disciples, and he went to the prison.
He saw seven guards standing at the prison gates, guarding it. Andrew prayed, and these guards fell down and died.
When he approached the prison gate, he traced the sign of the cross on it, and immediately the gate opened. When Andrew entered the prison with his disciples,
Matthew saw Andrew and immediately stood up. They greeted one another, and Andrew said to Matthew, “My brother, how did you come to be here?
For in three days the people of this city were going to bring you out and slaughter you for their food.
Where are the holy mysteries you learned? If you had spoken them, heaven and earth would have shaken.” Matthew answered
and said, “My brother Andrew, I heard our Lord say, ‘Look, I am sending you all out like lambs among wolves.’
For as soon as I entered this prison, I prayed before our Lord. He appeared to me and said, ‘Endure for twenty-seven days.
After that I will send Andrew to you, and he will bring you out of this prison, along with everyone who is with you.’
And just as our Lord promised me, here I have seen you today. Now what shall we do?” Then Andrew looked into the middle of the prison.
He saw the men imprisoned there, naked and eating grass like cattle. Andrew beat his breast and said:
“Our Lord Jesus Christ, look and see what they have given human beings, made in your image and likeness, to eat!” And the blessed man began to rebuke Satan, saying:
“Woe to you, Satan, enemy of our God and his angels! How long will you wage war against the human race?”
Andrew and Matthew knelt down and prayed. Afterward Andrew laid his hands on the eyes of those people who had been blinded.
Immediately they all saw the light. He also laid his hand on their hearts, and their minds were transformed and became like those of human beings. He said to them, “Go away
now to the lower part of the city. You will find a large fig tree along the road. Sit beneath it and eat its fruit
until I come to you. If I am delayed, you will find enough food on it to meet your needs.”
Those men answered and said to the blessed Andrew, “Come with us, my lord, lest the pagan people of this city see us again.”
And they will seize us and subject us to punishments worse than the former ones.” He said to them, “Go in peace. Truly I tell you,
when you go, not even a dog will bark at you.” Those men went away, just as the blessed Andrew had told them.
They numbered forty-nine. He told Matthew to go with his disciples
to the east of the city. Andrew prayed, and a cloud came down, took Matthew and his disciples, and set them on the mountain
where Peter the apostle was staying and teaching. They remained with him. Now when Andrew came out of the prison, he walked through the city
and saw a pillar with a bronze statue standing on top of it. He sat beside that pillar to see what would happen. And when the executioners went
to the prison to bring people out for their food, as was their daily custom, they found the prison doors open
and the guards dead, lying at the entrance. They returned to the rulers and told them, “We went to the prison
and found it open, with the guards dead and lying at the entrance. When we went inside, we found no one there.”
When the rulers heard this, they said to one another, “What is this thing that has happened? Could some people have entered the prison, killed the guards,
and taken away those who were imprisoned there?” When the rulers heard this, they said to one another, “What is this thing that has happened?
Could some people have entered the prison, killed the guards, and taken away those who were imprisoned there?”
Then the rulers said to the executioners, “Go to the prison and bring those seven guards,
so that we can eat them today. Immediately gather all the old men of the city for us, and let us cast lots among them.
We will slaughter those on whom the lot falls, seven each day, for our food, until we select young men and put them aboard a ship,
and they go to the regions around us, load people onto their ships, and bring them here to be food for us.”
The executioners went to the prison and brought those seven guards, who were dead.
There was an oven built in the middle of the city. Beside the fire was a large stone winepress. In this very press
they used to slaughter people. Their blood flowed and collected in that press, and they would draw out the blood and drink it.
When they brought those seven dead men, they arranged them on the press, ready to raise their hands and lift them up.
The blessed Andrew heard a voice saying to him, “Andrew, look and see what is being done in this city.”
And when he [?], he prayed and said, “Our Lord Jesus Christ, you who brought me to this city,
do not allow anything evil to happen in it. Instead, let the knives fall from the hands of these executioners.”
Immediately their hands became powerless, and they could neither raise nor lower them. When the rulers saw what had happened,
they wept bitterly, saying, “Woe to us! There are sorcerers here, and they are the ones who entered the prison.”
They killed the guards and brought out those who had been imprisoned there. And look, they have even made the executioners deaf. What are we to do now?
Then they said to the executioners, “Go and gather the old men of the city for us, because we are hungry.” So they went and gathered them.
They found [?] two hundred and sixteen and brought them to their rulers, who ordered them to cast lots.
The lot fell on seven old men. One of the old men on whom the lot had fallen spoke up and said to the executioners, “I beg
you: I have one young son. Take him and slaughter him in my place, and let me go.” They said to him, “We cannot do this.
But our rulers have given us orders.” The executioners went and were told, “If he provides someone in his place, let him go.”
The executioners informed that old man of this. The old man replied, “I also have a daughter.
Take her too, along with her brother, to be slaughtered, and let me go.” He handed them over to be slaughtered, and the executioners took these children away to slaughter them.
They wept and said, “Do not kill us while we are so young. Let us reach full maturity,
and then you can slaughter us.” There was also this custom in that city: they did not bury those who died,
but instead ate them. The executioners, however, were not persuaded by these children.
Instead, they took them away to the winepress where they used to slaughter people, intending to slaughter them.
When Saint Andrew saw this, he wept bitterly and said, “Our Lord Jesus Christ,
just as you listened to me, a sinner, concerning these dead people, and in your divinity did not allow them to be eaten, so
now do not allow them to proceed with killing these children. Instead, let their hands grow weak, and let the knives fall and melt like wax before a fire.”
The moment blessed Andrew prayed, the knives came loose and fell from the executioners’ hands.
When Saint Andrew saw what had happened, he praised God, who had answered him in everything. When the rulers saw what had happened,
they wept bitterly and said, “Alas for us! What are we to do now?” Satan took on the appearance of an old man
and stood among them and said, “Alas for you! What are you to do, since you have no food?
Now get up, seize a stranger in this city named Andrew, and kill him. He is the one who brought out those men who had been confined in prison.”
Saint Andrew watched Satan as he spoke from among the crowd, but Satan could not see the blessed man.
Christ’s apostle spoke up and said to Satan, “You enemy of all humanity, constantly fighting against it!
May our Lord Jesus Christ bring you down and cast you into the deep pit of destruction!” When Satan heard this, he said, “Oh, oh! It is you—I hear your voice,
but I do not know where you are.” The blessed man replied to Satan, “You truly are blind, and you cannot see
the holy ones.” When Satan heard this, he said to the crowd, “Look now for the man I am speaking with, and seize him!”
For he is the one obstructing your plans.” Those wicked men ran and shut the city gates.
They went around looking for the blessed Andrew throughout the city, but they could not find him. Then our Lord Jesus Christ appeared to him
and said to him, “Andrew, get up and show them your power, so that they may learn that the power of Satan, who dwells in them, is nothing.”
Then the blessed Andrew stood up before the whole crowd and said, “I am Andrew, the one you are looking for.”
Then all the people ran and seized him. They said to him, “We will do to you what you have done to us.” They began discussing among themselves, saying,
“What kind of death shall we put him to? If we cut off his head,” they said, “that is not a painful death. And if we burn him in a fire, that too is nothing.”
Then one of them, after Satan had entered him, spoke up and said to them, “Just as he has made us suffer, so we too should make him suffer.
Let us do this to him: let us wind ropes around his neck and drag him through the streets and ruins of this city. When he dies, we will divide his body among us all.” This pleased all the
people. They put ropes around his neck and dragged him through all the streets and ruins of the city,
until his body was torn by the stones over which he was being dragged, and his blood flowed like water. When evening came,
they threw him into prison with his hands bound behind his back. Again, when morning came, they brought him out
and put ropes around his neck and dragged him throughout the city. His whole body was torn against the ground.
The blessed man prayed in anguish and said, “Our Lord Jesus Christ, see what they are doing to me. I am enduring it because of your command.
For if it were not for your mercy, I would send them, together with their city, into a deep abyss.
But, my Lord, only do not let the enemy mock me.” When the blessed man said these things, Satan spoke from behind him and said to the people,
“Keep striking him on the mouth so that he cannot speak.” When evening came, they threw him into prison. Then Satan took with him
seven demons and entered the prison. They stood before Saint Andrew and mocked him, saying,
“Now you have been caught in our hands. Who will rescue you now? Look, you have been putting an end to our works in every city,
and you have destroyed our temples and the houses of the gods that were built for us.” Satan ordered those seven demons who were with him to kill the blessed man. Then,
when those demons approached and saw the seal of Christ between his eyes, they were afraid and fled from him. Satan spoke and said to them,
“Why did you run away from him? Who is he?” They said to him, “We cannot approach him because of the seal that is on him.
But you go and kill him, if you are so powerful.” Satan said to them, “Come, then, let us mock him.” Then those demons came with Satan, their chief,
and mocked the blessed man, saying, “Andrew, look! You have come to great disgrace and harsh judgment.”
Then, when the blessed Andrew heard these things, he said, “Even if you kill me, I will not do your will,
but the will of my Lord. For if my Lord comes to me in this city, I will punish you as you deserve.”
When the demons heard these things, they vanished from his presence like smoke.
When morning came, they brought the blessed Andrew out of prison, tied ropes around his neck, and dragged him along. Again his flesh and all the hair of his head were being torn out.
The blessed man cried out loudly with sobs and tears and said, “Our Lord Jesus Christ, I have had enough of these afflictions for three days, day and night,

from Satan, the demons, and these [?]. Give the command, my Lord, and receive my spirit, or show me your grace so that I may be strengthened.” As he said these things, a voice came to him in Hebrew, saying, “Andrew,
heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away. Now turn around and look at the flesh that was torn from you, and see what has become of it.”
He looked and saw large trees that had sprouted and borne fruit. Saint Andrew said,
“Now, my Lord, I know that you have not abandoned me.” When evening came, they threw him into prison, saying, “His body is ruined,
and tonight he will die.” Then our Lord Jesus Christ appeared to him in prison and said to him, “Andrew, give me your hand.” He took him by the hand, and immediately he stood up, completely well.
The blessed man fell down and worshiped him. Afterward he looked into the middle of the pit in which he was confined and saw a pillar called an alabastron in Greek.
Andrew stretched out his hand and said, “Mute stone, fear the sign of the cross, before which heaven and earth tremble.
Let abundant water immediately flow from your mouth, enough to flood this city.”
Immediately that pillar poured out abundant water like a mighty river. The water grew very strong and killed their children and their livestock.
They tried to flee from the city. Then the blessed Andrew prayed, and a cloud of fire came down
and surrounded the city like a [?], so that they could not flee. When Andrew learned what had happened,
he praised God and said, “I bless you, our Lord Jesus Christ.” All the inhabitants of the city trembled, weeping and saying,
“Woe to us! All these things have come upon us because of that stranger who is in prison.
Let us go and release him, so that we do not die a terrible death in these floodwaters and this fire.” They all came to the prison, crying out in a sobbing voice.
When the blessed Andrew saw that they had submitted themselves to him, he said to that pillar, “Enough now! Do not pour out any more water.
Look, I am going out to proclaim the word of God. And I tell you that if the inhabitants of this city believe, I will build a church in it
and remove you from here, take you there, and set you up in it, because you answered me and did what you were commanded.” At that very moment, that statue stopped pouring out water.
Andrew came out of the prison, and water flowed before his feet. Then the old man who had handed over his children to be slaughtered in his place approached him
and said to him, “Have mercy on us, our lord.” Andrew answered and said to him, “Have mercy on us, our lord.”
Andrew answered and said to him, “I ask you, how can you tell me to have mercy on you, when you had no mercy
on your children? For I tell you that in a little while these waters will go away and be swallowed up in the abyss.
And as for these executioners who used to slaughter people, you too will be swallowed up with them.” He turned and said to the crowd,
“Again, all of you, follow me.” As they went after him, the water parted to either side before the holy man’s feet.
Until he came to the place where that press stood. Blessed Andrew lifted his eyes to heaven.
He prayed, and the earth opened and swallowed the water, the torturers, and that old man. When the people of the city saw what had happened,
they began saying among themselves, “Woe to us! This man was sent here by God, and he will kill us because of the sufferings we made him endure.
For look, what happened to the torturers and that old man will happen to us.” When blessed Andrew heard this, he said to them,
“Do not be afraid, my children. God will not leave even these people in Sheol. They were snatched away to the earth below so that you might believe.”
Then Andrew ordered them to bring everyone who had drowned in the water.
But they could not bring them, because those who had died in the water were so many: men, women, children, and animals.
Then the blessed man prayed before God, and they all came back to life and stood up. After this he baptized them in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
He drew up a plan for a church for them, and it was quickly built. They brought the pillar that had poured out that water,
and set it up in the church. He laid down commandments and laws for them to observe.
He entrusted to them the mysteries of our Lord Jesus Christ, and instructed them to sow and support themselves by the sweat of their brows.
He was eager to leave them. They pleaded with him, from the least to the greatest, saying to him, “We beg you,
stay with us a few days. We are still newborn children in the faith, so that we may receive from your blessed spring and from your divine words.”
He would not be persuaded to stay with them, but went on his way. Then our Lord appeared to him in the form of a beautiful child,
and said to him, “Why are you going away and leaving them without fruit? Have you no pity on the newborn children who are coming after you, crying out?
Now return to the city and stay with them for seven days. When you enter the city, bring up those who were swallowed into the abyss.”
Then Andrew praised God and said, “Blessed are you, our Lord Jesus Christ, who do not want anyone to perish, but to live.”
He returned and entered the city. When the people of the city saw that he had come back, they rejoiced greatly. He spent seven days there,
teaching them and strengthening them in faith in our Lord. Then blessed Andrew prayed, and those men who had been swallowed into the abyss came back to life.
After seven days, all the people of the city went out, and from the least to the greatest they were showing him [?].
They cried out, saying, “One is the God of blessed Andrew, our Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of the living God,
to whom belong praise, worship, and thanksgiving, together with his blessed Father and his living and Holy Spirit, forever and ever. Amen.”
The account of Matthew and Andrew, when they made disciples in the city of Kalbin, which is Irqa, is finished.
